points.description: Chooses a paint color (any of the four) and describes how it would affect the inside of the doghouse in a way consistent with the experiment (e.g., light gray/white keeps the inside cooler; black/dark gray makes it warmer).
points.partial_credit: Half credit if a color is chosen but the effect on the inside temperature is missing or inconsistent with the data.

points.description: Supports the choice with specific experiment results, citing data that match the chosen color (e.g., white lid averaged 42°C, the lowest, vs. black 53°C; or black highest at 53°C if choosing warm), with a comparison to at least one other color.
points.partial_credit: Half credit if only a general trend is stated (e.g., lighter colors had lower temperatures) without specific values.

rubric.notes: Full marks: a chosen color, a consistent effect on the doghouse interior, and specific supporting data. Equivalent wording and either a cool (light) or warm (dark) rationale are accepted if consistent with the data. Zero for P2 if the data cited contradict the choice.
rubric.answer_key: Choose white (light gray also acceptable). A white doghouse would stay cooler inside because lighter colors absorb less energy from the sun. In the experiment, the white lid had the lowest average air temperature (42°C), compared with 53°C for black, 48°C for dark gray and 45°C for light gray, so white kept the air about 11°C cooler than black. A dark color is acceptable if the answer justifies it as a warmer doghouse with matching data (black 53°C).
